prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring the ubiquitin-proteasome system to a chosen protein and so remove it from the cell

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B014 alone, for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The unifying fact is structural. A small molecule, whether a designed bifunctional PROTAC or a thalidomide-type glue, creates a new interface between an E3 ligase and a protein that ligase would otherwise ignore, and ternary-complex structures show this directly for both. A citation worded around that principle, recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system by a small molecule, is honest for all three names: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated recruited degradation, and Handa identified cereblon as the direct target through which an existing drug acts by this same mechanism. This answers the chair's first question: one citation can cover both arms if it names the principle and not the compound class. The evidence is mature. The concept dates to 2001 and cereblon to 2010, independent laboratories have confirmed it across many ligases and targets, and glue-class drugs approved for patients are now mechanistically understood. Six of eight members already place B014 in their configuration, so the open matter is the third name, not the topic.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point. Three names leave out Ciulli (VHL ligands, first fully small-molecule VHL degraders, ternary-complex structure and structure-guided design), Sakamoto and Kim (co-authors of the 2001 paper), Ito (with Handa) and Gray. Handa's contribution is a target identification for an existing drug rather than a designed tool, so a reader can see this as two lineages joined by a citation. A PROTAC-only prize would be cleaner on credit but would be weakest on maturity, since no heterobifunctional degrader is yet approved. I accept that both configurations leave out real contributors, and I weigh the cost of that omission as lower than the cost of a prize that ignores the arm with approved drugs.

responses.point: Aili keeps Ciulli for the structural grounding of ternary complexes and says Handa's pillar is mainly a target-identification story, so the citation wording must be settled before the names.
responses.response: I agree the wording must come first, and I have proposed it above: the principle is recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system by a small molecule. On that wording Handa's work is more than target identification, because cereblon is the E3 ligase surface that the drug reshapes, and it is the first demonstration that this mechanism was already operating in a drug used in patients. That is a discovery the other two names do not imply. Ciulli's contribution to structure-guided optimisation is real, and I weigh it most heavily for the PROTAC arm. My judgement is that it extends a design concept already credited to Crews and Deshaies, while Handa adds a separate mechanism with clinical validation. I have not moved to Ciulli, though I would not call his case weak.

responses.point: Linke, who also names Crews, Deshaies and Handa, asks whether two pillars can share one citation and whether ternary-complex structural work is enough to justify Ciulli over Handa.
responses.response: Yes on the first: if the citation names the principle, not the compound class, both pillars fit. On the second, the ternary-complex structures are the best evidence for the principle, but they are the shared explanation for both arms and are not owned by one name. The VHL-BRD4 structure supports PROTAC design, and cereblon-ligand structures show the glue mechanism equally well. That is why I do not treat structure alone as a reason to favour Ciulli. Since you pressed on Sakamoto, I will answer: I would still prefer not to name him, because the committee has to pick the conceptual core and I read that as Crews and Deshaies. I recognise that this reasoning is imperfect and that his claim from the 2001 paper is not trivial.

responses.point: Chabes pairs a Crews and Deshaies PROTAC part with a second part for Liu's base editing, to keep the Liu credit clean and to leave a seat open.
responses.response: The credit logic is attractive, but I do not accept the second part. Base editing remains my first alternative and I regard Liu's chemistry as real, but the 2020 prize on programmable genome targeting still lies close to it, and the Nishida-Kondo priority question that you say you have not checked is unresolved. Two chemical-biology parts in a single year would also narrow the prize without adding evidence. A PROTAC-only first part also removes the arm with approved drugs, which in my view is the strongest maturity argument we have. I would rather keep B014 broad and wait for B042 than make a stronger case for it on a weaker one.

responses.point: Aqvist values the quantitative link between ternary-complex thermodynamics and degradation and the precise three-name PROTAC unit of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, but concedes the glue lineage is omitted and a careful reader will notice.
responses.response: I agree with the quantitative point, since cooperativity and ternary-complex stability are central to design for both arms. I would also note that your concession is the thing that bothers me about the Ciulli trio: by your own account the prize would leave out the lineage that already has approved drugs, and the omission becomes visible as soon as the citation is read. My trio fixes this by including Handa, at the cost of leaving out Ciulli. Both choices drop someone, but mine does not leave the main clinical validation outside the citation.

responses.point: Brzezinski continues to favour Gray and Winkler's electron transfer and lists B014 as an alternative.
responses.response: The mechanism is physically well-defined and I accept the evidence is complete, but he himself concedes that it builds on Marcus theory and the work on natural proteins by Dutton, and that it has had little reach beyond biophysics. I would not oppose B025 at a later date, but it should not take the place of a candidate that six members support and that has changed what chemists attempt.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name remains a genuine judgement between two lineages, and I could accept either trio if the committee settles on it with a citation that states the principle.
Whether the principle-based citation is read as too broad to tie to a precise discovery.

Whether the committee will want clinical approval of a heterobifunctional degrader before recognition; I think a few more years would cost little, but I do not think they are needed for the principle.
Whether the omission of Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Ito and Gray will be treated as an unavoidable limit of the three-name rule or as a flaw in the prize.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged. No conflict requires recusal for B014 or for either alternative. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the secretary, Peter Brzezinski, who is not a candidate. My own field is electron crystallography and porous materials, none of which is on this shortlist, though B054 (halide perovskites) is a materials topic on which I have no direct involvement.
